claims.location: source name rows 1-48
claims.evidence: samplenames.xls and mqpar.xml group the 24 DiD runs into 4 MaxQuant experiments plus_01, minus_01, plus_02, minus_02 (6 gel-slice fractions each). Paper: donor HS-5 cells SILAC-heavy labelled and DiD-stained, co-cultured 24 h with GFP K-562 acceptor cells, acceptor cells FACS-sorted into DiD+ and DiD- subpopulations; "This experiment was performed in duplicate". Each sorted-cell lysate is one physical sample; its two SILAC channels are given two source names (light = the acceptor K-562 proteome, heavy = HS-5-derived proteins inside the same K-562 cells) because they describe material of different cellular origin and the row coordinate (source, replicate, fraction) must be unique. The two names of a pair are channels of one lysate, not two samples.

claims.location: comment[label] + characteristics[protein origin] + characteristics[cell line] rows with comment[label] = SILAC light (24 rows: 1-6, 13-18, 25-30, 37-42)
claims.evidence: Paper Methods: "Donor cells were labeled with heavy isotopologues of lysine and arginine"; acceptor CML cells (K-562 GFP) were not labelled. Results: "Liquid chromatography-tandem MS enabled to identify heavy-labeled proteins within the proteome of acceptor cells". Data: in all four experiments light intensity is 98.4-99.5% of summed L+H intensity (hl_summary.txt), i.e. the light channel is the bulk acceptor proteome.

claims.location: comment[label] + characteristics[protein origin] + characteristics[cell line] rows with comment[label] = SILAC heavy (24 rows: 7-12, 19-24, 31-36, 43-48)
claims.evidence: Paper: donor HS-5 stromal cells labelled with L-lysine 13C6 15N2 and L-arginine 13C6 15N4 for 9 days; "In both samples, heavy proteins transferred from donor stromal cells, were identified." mqpar.xml: multiplicity 2, labelMods [light] / [Arg10;Lys8]. Heavy channel identity is therefore the cell of origin (HS-5), measured inside sorted K-562 cells; cell-line metadata on heavy rows (HS-5, CVCL_3720, bone marrow stroma, male 30Y) describes the protein donor.

claims.location: characteristics[sorted cell population] + factor value[sorted cell population] rows 1-48
claims.value: DiD positive (plus_01, plus_02); DiD negative (minus_01, minus_02)
claims.evidence: Experiment names plus_/minus_ (samplenames.xls, mqpar.xml) correspond to the paper's DiD+ / DiD- sorted acceptor subpopulations ("sorting of acceptor cells into two subpopulations: positive and negative for transferred vesicles (DiD+ vs DiD-)"). Data check: plus_ experiments carry more heavy (donor-derived) material than minus_ (H/(L+H) 1.62% / 1.20% vs 0.55% / 0.57%; heavy-detected protein groups in both replicates 969 plus vs 808 minus at >=2 unique peptides), matching the paper's 646 DiD+ vs 481 DiD- donor-derived proteins (Fig. 7a). The absolute numbers differ because the deposited search is MaxQuant 1.6.0.1 while the paper reports 1.5.3.12.

limitations: DUPLICATE: PXD013504 (cited by the paper's Data Availability) contains the same 24 DiD .raw files, SHA-1-identical, plus loose MaxQuant tables; it adds no runs. PXD011013 is the superset and is the annotated canonical deposit; recorded as a new group in annotations/DUPLICATES.md. PXD013504's proteinGroups.txt/parameters.txt are used here as evidence (same search).

PARTIAL SCOPE: 8 of 32 deposited .raw files are excluded: 710072209zar_k562_A, 710072210zar_k562_B, 710072211zar_k562IM_A, 710072212zar_k562IM_B, 710072213zar_HS5_A, 710072214zar_HS5_B, 710072215zar_HS5IM_A, 710072216zar_HS5IM_B (.raw). They are single-shot in-solution digests (Q Exactive + nanoAcquity) of K-562 and HS-5 +/- imatinib; samplenames.xls says the +IM runs are "not discussed in this manuscript". They were searched in MaxQuant parameter group 0 with multiplicity 2 (Arg10;Lys8) but nothing documents any SILAC labelling of these samples: light is 98.1-99.3% of L+H intensity even in HS-5 runs, so no heavy-labelled material is evident and the heavy channel has no documented identity (batch rule 7). Recorded in BLOCKED.md.

Trans-SILAC channel encoding: the light and heavy rows of one run are two channels of ONE physical sorted-K-562 lysate. Heavy rows carry the HS-5 cell-line metadata because the heavy label marks protein of HS-5 origin; the physical sample (sorted K-562 GFP+ acceptor cells) is stated in characteristics[co-culture]/[sorted cell population]/[protein origin]. There is no curated precedent for trans-SILAC in sdrf-annotated-datasets.

Paper says MaxQuant 1.5.3.12; the deposited mqpar/parameters.txt are MaxQuant 1.6.0.1 (PRIDE data protocol also says 1.6.0.1). The SDRF follows the deposited search; heavy-protein counts recomputed from the deposit (969 DiD+ / 808 DiD-) differ from the paper's 646 / 481.
plus_01 and minus_01 (and _02) are presumed to be the two subpopulations sorted from the same co-culture (paper: acceptor cells sorted "into two subpopulations"); not stated per file.

comment[reduction reagent] / comment[alkylation reagent] = not available: the paper names TCEP / iodoacetamide for the in-solution digest, but the DiD samples went through in-gel digestion "according to standard protocols" (Shevchenko 2007) without naming reagents.
characteristics[culture medium] = not available: maintenance medium is RPMI for both lines, but the SILAC labelling medium base and the co-culture medium are not named.
characteristics[passage number] = not available; K-562 cell type = not available.
Precursor tolerance = MaxQuant main-search 4.5 ppm (first search 20 ppm).
